evidence_claims.claim: Jerusalem is retained as a point-control anchor only. Jerusalem was the royal center in 1130; this supports a city anchor, not a continuous border.
Damascus is retained as a point-control anchor only. Damascus was the center of an active Burid polity in 1130; frontier relations do not imply a precise boundary.
Ascalon is retained only as a disputed 1130 scenario anchor. The available locators do not yet meet the page-level standard for the reviewed baseline.
Tripoli is retained as the county center in 1130. The claim is limited to the city; it does not establish a county footprint.
Tortosa is plausible as part of the county core, but the reviewed pages do not independently establish this point for 1130. It enters only the inclusive scenario.
Antioch is retained as a point-control anchor only. Antioch identifies the principality core in 1130; the city anchor does not define its perimeter.
Edessa is retained at reduced model weight. The evidence names Joscelin as count of Edessa in the adjacent 1131 narrative, so the one-year bridge remains an explicit uncertainty.
Cairo is a plausible Ayyubid political center, but the reviewed page names Egypt rather than Cairo. It enters only the inclusive scenario.
Damascus is retained as an Ayyubid political-center anchor. A page-addressable scholarly account styles Saladin sultan of Damascus in the 1187 narrative; no imperial perimeter follows from the point.
Jerusalem is retained as a point-control anchor only. Jerusalem was under Ayyubid control by the end-of-year 1187 convention.
Acre is retained as a point-control anchor because the reviewed Ibn Shaddad pages name its 1187 capture or surrender. The point does not establish a coastal polygon.
Jaffa remains unverified in the reviewed primary-source pages. It is excluded from the reviewed baseline and retained only in the inclusive scenario.
Ascalon is retained as a point-control anchor because the reviewed Ibn Shaddad pages name its 1187 capture or surrender. The point does not establish a coastal polygon.
Gaza is retained as a point-control anchor because the reviewed Ibn Shaddad pages name its 1187 capture or surrender. The point does not establish a coastal polygon.
Sidon is retained as a point-control anchor because the reviewed Ibn Shaddad pages name its 1187 capture or surrender. The point does not establish a coastal polygon.
Beirut is retained as a point-control anchor because the reviewed Ibn Shaddad pages name its 1187 capture or surrender. The point does not establish a coastal polygon.
Tyre is retained as a point-control anchor only. Tyre remained a Latin coastal holdout at end-1187; it is modeled as a point remnant.
Tripoli is retained as a surviving Latin city at the end of 1187. The evidence does not establish the county's inland extent.
Antioch is retained as a surviving Latin city at the end of 1187. The evidence does not establish the principality's surrounding lordships.
Generalized Mount Lebanon geometry for display and sensitivity testing only.
Generalized Taurus geometry for display and sensitivity testing only.

payload.paraphrase: Antioch identifies the principality core in 1130; the city anchor does not define its perimeter.
payload.verification_note: The dated succession crisis explicitly concerns Antioch, entry into the city, and custody of the principality after Bohemond II; no perimeter is inferred.

payload.paraphrase: Jerusalem was under Ayyubid control by the end-of-year 1187 convention.
payload.verification_note: The surrender and transfer of possession on 2 October 1187 are explicit.

payload.verification_note: The date and capture of Acre are explicit.

payload.paraphrase: Sidon and Beirut were named captured centers after Hattin; the points do not authorize a smoothed coast polygon.
payload.verification_note: The narrative explicitly reports the capture of both centers.

payload.paraphrase: Ascalon and Gaza were named captured centers after Hattin; the points do not authorize a smoothed coast polygon.
payload.verification_note: The narrative explicitly reports the capture of Ascalon and the surrender of Gaza.

payload.paraphrase: Tyre remained a Latin coastal holdout at end-1187; it is modeled as a point remnant.
payload.verification_note: The source describes the concentration of Franks at Tyre, the subsequent failed siege, and the siege continuing through 30 December 1187.

payload.paraphrase: Tripoli remained a surviving northern Latin center after Hattin; inland limits remain a gap.
payload.verification_note: Tripoli is an explicit refuge immediately after Hattin. This page alone does not establish its full end-of-year status or inland extent.

payload.paraphrase: At Hattin Saladin is styled sultan of Egypt, Damascus, and Aleppo. This supports Damascus as a political center; Egypt does not by itself establish a Cairo city-control point.
payload.verification_note: The page names Damascus in Saladin's title. Cairo is not named.
